clue.text: Saw, only to become a prisoner

definitions.meaning: past tense of see, meaning looked at or witnessed
to be detained or kept in custody, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed something, only to find themselves locked up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE HELD, the word means to be taken into custody; whole, it is the past tense of behold.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an old verb for look at, so its past tense is a synonym of saw.

clue.text: They may call for you at an American hotel

definitions.text: They may call for you at an American hotel

parts.words: They may call for you at an American hotel
parts.note: hotel porters in the US come to your room when called, or call out names in the lobby; 'call for' also suggests fetching a guest

explanation.surface: A traveller's note about who might come knocking at a US hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is American for hotel porters, who carry luggage and run errands; 'call for you' covers both calling at your door and being called by you.
explanation.definitionFit: American hotels employ uniformed porters who collect guests and luggage, the staff the clue describes.

clue.text: Up to now, best-seller is followed by other novel

parts.note: a best-seller is a hit

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of other are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Until today, a best-selling book has always had a follow-up novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book in a publishing surface, but it is the anagram signal: OTHER becomes HERTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal adverb meaning until this time, a synonym of so far.

clue.text: Very small part for an actor, but it's a job

definitions.text: Very small part for an actor
definitions.meaning: a bit part may give an actor a single spoken sentence
as in one's ... of work, an occupation

explanation.surface: An actor grumbles that a tiny role is still work.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor with one sentence to say has a single speech in the script; a trade or occupation is one's line of business.

clue.text: Don't weary everyone being boring

parts.note: to weary only part of a group, not all of them, is to tire a portion of them
not everyone means only a portion of people

explanation.surface: Advice to a speaker: don't bore everybody by being dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, 'Don't weary everyone' says weary only a portion: TIRE + SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearisome or tedious is boring, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: News that the teacher would welcome in any form?

definitions.text: the teacher would welcome in any form
definitions.meaning: a teacher wants brains in every class, a form being a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A question of what tidings a teacher would be glad to hear in whatever shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' is a British school class, so the second reading is cleverness in any class of pupils, not news in any format.
explanation.definitionFit: Military or secret information is called by this name, and so is the cleverness a teacher hopes pupils have.

clue.text: Extremely nervous?

parts.note: jittery, and punningly to do with the edges or extremes of something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' suggests very, but also hints at being at the extremities, the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means being tense and jumpy, so this adjective means nervous.

clue.text: Speak freely and reveal what's there

definitions.meaning: to talk candidly about one's feelings
to unlock or uncover something so its contents are visible

explanation.surface: A therapist urges a client to talk frankly and show what lies within.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to confide candidly and to unfasten something so its insides are exposed.

clue.text: They play supporting roles in the studio

definitions.text: They play supporting roles in the studio

parts.words: They play supporting roles in the studio
parts.note: stands that literally support canvases in an artist's studio, posing as actors in minor roles

explanation.surface: Seems to describe actors with minor parts in a film studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting roles' and 'studio' suggest film or theatre; the studio is a painter's and the support is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters prop canvases on these wooden stands while working, so they literally support the art.

clue.text: Hidden talent for demolition

indicators.note: something marked for demolition will be knocked down and rebuilt, so the letters of talent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A talent kept concealed, perhaps headed for ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for demolition' tells you to break up TALENT and rebuild its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant or not yet shown, like an undeveloped ability, is concealed.

clue.text: Vertigo surprises

definitions.meaning: a disease of livestock causing giddiness, and a word for dizziness
as a verb, astonishes or amazes

explanation.surface: Dizziness that comes as a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for a giddy reeling condition, and also the verb meaning astounds.

clue.text: Settled after fresh start somewhere in N America

indicators.note: after places the word for settled behind the other pieces

parts.note: fresh means new
to start a company or college is to found it
a bird that has settled has come down to land

explanation.surface: Colonists settled somewhere in North America after a new beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Settled' as colonists making a home; here it means came to rest, as a bird does, and 'after' puts that word last.
explanation.definitionFit: A large island and province of eastern Canada, so a place in North America.

clue.text: That man heads the Spanish list

indicators.note: heads means goes in front of, so the pronoun comes first

parts.note: that man is he
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A man tops a list of Spanish names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' is the nautical verb, a ship leaning to one side, not a roll of names; 'heads' means goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans over to one side is said to heel, a nautical synonym of list.

clue.text: Beautiful girl one may ring, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for the thing rung is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a bell is something one rings

explanation.surface: A lovely girl someone might telephone, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests telephoning the girl, but it is a bell that is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived word for a beauty, especially the most attractive woman at a gathering.

clue.text: Winger who is easily outwitted

definitions.meaning: a winged creature, here a seabird

explanation.surface: A wide footballer who is easily fooled by the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer on the wing, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabird has wings; as a noun the word also means a gullible person or dupe.

clue.text: Neat residences

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so these are homes for cows, not tidy houses

explanation.surface: Looks like tidy homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but it is an archaic word for cattle; the answer is a Scottish and northern word for cowsheds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowsheds house cattle, which were once called neat, so they are cattle residences.

clue.text: Don't allow untidy beard

indicators.note: an untidy beard has its letters messed up, so the word beard is rearranged

explanation.surface: A dress code banning a scruffy beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' scrambles BEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude or prohibit someone formally, so to refuse to permit.

clue.text: Spiteful functionary, one with position on board

parts.note: petty means small-minded and spiteful
a functionary is an official or officer

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited bureaucrat, perhaps on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a boardroom, but it means aboard ship: a naval rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval non-commissioned rank, so someone with a post aboard ship.

clue.text: Symphonist, British, is turning up with English composer needing no introduction

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the words British and is are read bottom to top
with no introduction means the composer's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Frederick Delius was an English composer

explanation.surface: A British symphonist coming into vogue alongside an English composer who is so famous he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses B IS to SIB; 'needing no introduction' cuts the D from DELIUS. The answer is the Finnish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Sibelius, the Finnish composer, wrote seven symphonies and is a celebrated symphonist.

clue.text: This can provide an image that includes love — for oneself?

definitions.text: This can provide an image that includes love — for oneself?

indicators.note: includes means the letter for love is put within the other letters
can provide signals that the letters given can be rearranged to supply another word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Self-love: projecting an image of yourself that you adore.
explanation.walkthrough: AN IMAGE with O (love, a tennis score of nothing) inside is rearranged; the whole clue also describes excessive self-regard.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive preoccupation with oneself, which is love directed at oneself.

clue.text: Creating pure liquid is improving

indicators.note: liquid means flowing and unfixed, so the letters of creating pure are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making a clean drink is good for one's health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' looks like part of the drink scene but mixes CREATING PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting better in health after illness, so getting well again.

clue.text: Medical man imprisoned for harmless frolic

indicators.note: for joins the jailed doctor to the result; the holding-inside idea really comes from imprisoned itself, read as being in a prison

parts.note: imprisoned means put in gaol, the old British spelling of jail, so the word supplies the prison that holds the doctor
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor locked up just for some innocent fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' does double duty: it is GAOL, the British spelling of jail, and also tells you the medical man sits inside it; 'for' merely leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful skip or leap, so an innocent bit of fun.

clue.text: Not well employed?

definitions.meaning: split as two words, ... means working for a company

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, IN FIRM means working for a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak or sickly through age or illness, so in poor health.

clue.text: Expert seen about new ailment

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the expert's letters go round the abbreviation

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist examining a newly reported illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ACE around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition causing spots, a minor complaint and so an ailment.

clue.text: Order of letters in the dictionary

indicators.note: letters in tells you the answer is some of the letters inside the words the dictionary

explanation.surface: Seems to describe alphabetical order in a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order of letters' looks like alphabetical order; 'Order' is the definition, a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by authority is an official command or order.

clue.text: Bit of light timber

definitions.meaning: a ray or shaft of light
a long heavy piece of wood in a building

explanation.surface: A piece of lightweight wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' reads as lightweight with timber, but it is illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of sunlight is a ray, and a structural wooden joist or girder is a length of timber.

clue.text: Not unlike a spill of ink

indicators.note: a spill scatters something, so the letters of a and ink are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Something resembling an ink blot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spill of' rearranges A INK.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar or related in character, so resembling.

clue.text: List of items available for males thought socially acceptable

parts.note: males are men
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable, from the old British U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: A list of things on offer to men deemed respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U was a 1950s British label for upper-class versus lower-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant card or computer list showing the choices on offer.

clue.text: Criticism for decent chap leading strike

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the chap's word comes first

parts.note: a brick is old British slang for a reliable, good-hearted person
to bat is to hit

explanation.surface: A good fellow leading a walkout attracts complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but means hit; 'a brick' is dated British slang for a good sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of harsh criticism, originally a missile thrown in anger.

clue.text: Quit school subject and make one's name as a writer

parts.note: RE is religious education, a subject in British schools

parts.words: make one's name as a writer
parts.note: to sign is to write your name

explanation.surface: A teacher leaves their subject to become a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make one's name' sounds like becoming famous but means writing a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down from a job is to leave or give it up.

clue.text: Article seen in French newspaper — it's refreshing

indicators.note: seen in means the article is placed inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading Paris daily newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece in a French paper hailed as refreshing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece but is A, inside LE MONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool citrus soft drink, something that refreshes.

clue.text: Country where you may see us in exotic sari

indicators.note: in places us inside the rearranged sari
exotic means strange and unusual, so sari is rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller spots people like us wearing an exotic sari abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the sari to RSIA, and 'in' sets the word us inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest nation on Earth, spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.
